findings.title: Google Meet fallback crashes when destinationCalendar is empty
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` produces an empty array when no destination calendar is set, so `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined. The next line dereferences `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration`, throwing a TypeError before the intended fallback to Daily can run. Previously `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` was safely undefined. Use optional chaining, e.g. `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

findings.title: updateLocation creates booking references without externalCalendarId or credentialId
findings.body: `referencesToCreate` now reads `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`, but `CalendarManager.updateEvent` does not return either field (unlike `createEvent`). After editing a location, the newly created calendar `BookingReference` rows will have null `externalCalendarId` and null `credentialId`. Later cancellation/reschedule/update logic cannot identify the external calendar or credential, so it may target the wrong calendar or fail to delete/update the right event. Either `updateEvent` should return these fields, or `updateLocation` should derive them from the calendar reference being updated.

findings.title: Google updateEvent fallback calendar lookup always misses
findings.body: When `externalCalendarId` is falsy, the fallback is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, which compares each calendar's externalId against null/undefined and returns undefined. `calendar.events.update` is then called with an undefined calendarId instead of the previous behavior of using `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`. The same broken pattern appears in `deleteEvent` around line 317. Legacy bookings or references without `externalCalendarId` will fail to update/delete Google Calendar events.

findings.title: Google Meet description patch uses undefined calendarId when no selected calendar
findings.body: `calendar.events.insert` uses `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the subsequent `calendar.events.patch` uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar` without that fallback. When no destination in the array matches the current credentialId, `selectedCalendar` is undefined; the insert proceeds against primary, but the patch that adds the hangout link fails because the calendarId is undefined. Use the same fallback in both calls.

findings.title: Office365 createEvent always targets the first destination calendar
findings.body: Even though EventManager now iterates all destination calendars and calls `createEvent` once per credential, Office365 still destructures only the first element of `event.destinationCalendar` and ignores the supplied credentialId. For a collective event with multiple hosts, every Office365 invocation targets the same first host calendar, causing duplicate events in that calendar and no event in the other hosts' Office365 calendars. The service must select the destination whose credentialId matches the current credential, similar to GoogleCalendarService. LarkCalendarService and BaseCalendarService have the same first-element-only behavior.

findings.title: Team destination calendars are dropped when organizer has no destinationCalendar
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer user has a destination calendar. The team calendars are then added with `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`, which is a no-op on null. If the organizer has no destination calendar but the other collective hosts do, all collected `teamDestinationCalendars` are lost and EventManager falls back to the organizer's first connected calendar rather than creating events in the hosts' selected calendars. Initialize `evt.destinationCalendar` to an array before pushing or assign the combined array explicitly.

findings.title: Confirmed collective bookings only schedule the first destination calendar
findings.body: When a booking requiring confirmation is later confirmed, this handler rebuilds `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` from `booking.destinationCalendar` (a single Prisma relation) or the confirming user's default. The multi-host `teamDestinationCalendars` assembled at initial booking time are not persisted or reconstructed here. `handleConfirmation`/EventManager therefore creates calendar events only for the first destination, not for all hosts of a collective event.

findings.title: Paid collective bookings schedule only the first destination calendar
findings.body: Both `getBooking` and `handlePaymentSuccess` build `evt.destinationCalendar` from the booking's single `destinationCalendar` or the user default. For a paid collective event, the multi-host destination calendars assembled in `handleNewBooking` are not available here and are not stored on the booking. When payment succeeds and `EventManager.create` runs, only the first/primary calendar receives the event; other hosts are not scheduled. The same issue exists in `paypal-webhook.ts`.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation still deletes only one organizer calendar reference
findings.body: Inside the new loop over `bookingCalendarReference`, the recurring/allRemaining branch ignores the current reference's `credentialId` and instead maps over `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` (the organizer's own credentials). For each updated booking it then calls `references.find(...)`, which returns only the first calendar reference. For a collective recurring booking with multiple host calendars, this repeats deletion of the first organizer-visible event and never deletes events belonging to the other host references. It should iterate all calendar references and use each reference's credential/externalCalendarId.

findings.title: Organization creation slug condition is inverted
findings.body: The diff changes `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, and similarly changes `requestedSlug` in the metadata. This is the opposite of the previous logic and is unrelated to the destinationCalendar change. With billing disabled, new organizations no longer receive a slug, likely breaking org creation/URLs; with billing enabled, slug is now set when it was previously withheld in favor of requestedSlug. Revert this condition unless there is a separate intentional billing change.

findings.title: All Google calendar events use the first destination as organizer
findings.body: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is always the first element of `event.destinationCalendar`, and its externalId is used as the organizer email for every create/update invocation. When EventManager iterates the other host destination calendars with different credentialIds, the event is inserted into another host's calendar but the organizer attendee is still set to the first host's externalId. This can set the wrong organizer/permissions or cause Google to reject the event. The organizer email should correspond to the destination/credential being processed.
